audit_findings.title: Post-acquisition debt interest is absent from the FY2025 owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $470.0 million term loan; computed annual interest of approximately $21.3 million pre-tax at 4.53%; Leonard Valve contributed $9.9 million of pre-tax earnings for the first six months of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE anchor omits both Leonard Valve's earnings and the interest, maintenance investment, and working-capital requirements associated with its acquisition financing.
audit_findings.evidence: The acquisition was funded under a new three-year, $470 million term loan with a group of eight banks.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch rather than merely a possible error: the valuation combines pre-acquisition FY2025 OE with the post-acquisition balance sheet and share count. The omitted acquisition earnings increase value, while the omitted financing and investment requirements decrease it. The $470 million transaction equals about 7.7% of the $6.098 billion base operating value, so a complete treatment is reasonably capable of affecting the valuation conclusion even though the disclosed first-half earnings and computed loan interest are similar in scale.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE from post-acquisition results, retaining the term-loan interest and incorporating Leonard Valve's eligible D&A, maintenance capex, and working-capital needs; then rerun every scenario without separately deducting debt principal.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may include cash that is not freely distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: $181.3 million bridge balance; computed maximum effect of $1.31 per share if the entire balance were removed
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash that is restricted, operationally necessary, or subject to repatriation leakage should be excluded from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, approximately $140 million of cash and marketable securities were held by our foreign subsidiaries, substantially all of which were located in China.
audit_findings.explanation: The restriction is unresolved because the $140.1 million foreign-cash disclosure is from December 2025, while the bridge uses June 2026 cash after $38 million of first-half repatriation. Nevertheless, even removing all $181.3 million—an intentionally conservative ceiling—would reduce values to approximately $37.40, $44.18, and $49.33 per share. Each remains below the $60.48 market price, so this issue cannot reverse the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 jurisdictional cash schedule and quantify restricted, operational, and tax-leakage amounts; revise the bridge only if distributable cash is needed for a more precise value estimate.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition earn-out obligations may be an omitted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid contingent purchase-price liability would be a non-operating claim requiring deduction in the equity bridge unless its settlement cost is already captured consistently in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company also agreed to make contingent payments based on the amount by which sales of products increase over the next three years .
audit_findings.explanation: The 2024 filing demonstrates that contingent payments were contractually agreed, but the supplied June 2026 record does not identify their fair value, maximum exposure, payment probability, or whether they are included within accrued or other liabilities. The claim may reduce common-equity value, but the record cannot establish its magnitude or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the acquisition accounting workpapers and June 2026 accrued-liability and other-liability detail for the earn-out's recognized fair value, maximum contractual payout, settlement dates, and any OE effects; deduct only the unpaid amount not otherwise captured.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may retain a nonrecurring tax benefit
audit_findings.mechanism: If included in FY2025 OE, the one-time cash-tax benefit inflates the $434.0 million anchor and is capitalized through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash provided by operations in 2025 was $616.8 million and higher than $581.8 million in 2024, primarily as a result of higher earnings and a one-time tax adjustment related to a tax law change that benefited 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that a one-time tax adjustment benefited 2025 operating cash flow, but it does not establish that the adjustment entered the OE calculation or state its amount. Any correction can only reduce the current scenario values. Because even the uncorrected bull value of $50.64 is $9.84 per share below the $60.48 market price, removing the benefit cannot reverse the present overvaluation conclusion, although it could lower the reported values.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $434.0 million FY2025 OE build through current taxes, deferred taxes, and working-capital adjustments; remove the specifically identified one-time amount if included, but rerun only to refine the downside values.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: computed residuals of approximately $13.7 million in 2017, $14.3 million in 2018, $12.6 million in 2023, and $12.7 million in 2024; zero effect on the selected $434.0 million anchor under the stated MIN(trend, latest) rule
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A would be added back to historical OE and could affect the trend calculation, but it does not enter the latest-year anchor directly.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2017 $56.4m (80.5% of filed D&A); FY2018 $57.6m (80.1% of filed D&A); FY2023 $65.7m (83.9% of filed D&A); FY2024 $66.1m (83.9% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is demonstrably conservative, not an overstatement. Even if every listed residual were eligible, the valuation still selects FY2025 OE because the stated $505 million trend exceeds the $434 million latest-year ceiling. Accordingly, these historical adjustments cannot change the current anchor or scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual components from the relevant depreciation and amortization notes before using historical OE for a future trend-based anchor; no current valuation rerun is required unless a qualifying FY2025 residual is identified.
